findings.issue: The non-finite check runs AFTER the optimizer update in all four loops (CONTRACTS.md: "A non-finite training batch loss raises DivergedError(step)"; the task says "for LBFGS check after the step", i.e. before the step everywhere else). In train_loop_svd the per-sample losses come back at :720, optimizer.step(batch) consumes them at :722, and _record_train_batch only checks at :736 — so a NaN Gram is handed to Sven's eigh/SVD first. Same in train_loop_hig (:790 loss -> :792 step -> :795 check) and train_loop_jd (:856 -> :859 -> :862). Consequence: exactly the blow-ups F6 named ("Sven / HIG / KFAC blow-ups raise in a linalg call") keep surfacing as an unclassified RuntimeError/LinAlgError instead of DivergedError(step), so diverged_at_step is lost for the Sven/HIG families and C-R1's classifier has to keep guessing from message strings. For LBFGS the step index is also off by one (probe: LBFGS lr=1e30 reports step 2, the line search went non-finite during step 1).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `_check_finite(mean, step)` call immediately after the loss is computed and before the update in the non-closure branch of train_loop_standard (:630), in train_loop_svd (between :720 and :722), train_loop_hig (between :790 and :792) and train_loop_jd (between :856 and :859); keep the existing post-step check only for `uses_closure`. The `.item()` is already needed by the online curve, so there is no extra sync in the svd/hig/jd loops.

findings.issue: evaluate() enforces its advertised invariants ("eval mode, restores the previous mode, mutates no buffer") only when forward_fn is an nn.Module: `module = forward_fn if isinstance(forward_fn, nn.Module) else None`, and _eval_context(None) is a no-op. train_loop_svd (:699, :740, :743) and train_loop_hig (:773, :799, :802) both pass a bound `model.evaluate`, so for the two loops where F2/F3 actually happened the guarantee is delegated entirely to the sven repo with no defence in depth and no test in this track. Probe with a wrapper whose evaluate forgets eval mode: evaluate() mutated 27 buffers (bn1.running_mean/var/num_batches_tracked, ...) and silently used batch statistics — i.e. a regression in sven_wrapper.py reintroduces F2 with every loops-track test still green. (SvenWrapper._eval_mode in the current sven tree is correct, so this is latent, not live.)
findings.suggested_fix: In evaluate(), resolve the module defensively: `owner = getattr(forward_fn, "__self__", None); module = forward_fn if isinstance(forward_fn, nn.Module) else (getattr(owner, "model", None) if owner is not None else None)` and pass that to _eval_context (idempotent with the wrapper's own _eval_mode). Add a test with a deliberately-wrong wrapper asserting no buffer moves.

findings.issue: Curve-key deviation from CONTRACTS.md ("Per-batch keys keep their names") that no downstream file knows about. `val_batch`, `batch_times_val` and `avg_batch_time_val` are gone (legacy eu_old.py:259,274,290); the replacements `eval_times` / `avg_eval_time` appear nowhere outside experiment_utils.py and are not in CONTRACTS.md. Stale name lists: analysis/style.py:453 OUTCOME_COLUMNS and analysis/scan_analysis.py:928 STANDALONE_QUANTITIES still rank timing on 'avg_batch_time_val'/'avg_epoch_time', generic_scan.py:151 _DIAG_LOSS_KEYS still names 'val_batch'/'batch_times_val'. Worse for the timing story: `epoch_times` now contains the end-of-epoch evaluation of THREE splits (val + test + train_eval, ~5x the old eval cost on CIFAR), so `avg_epoch_time` is no longer a training-speed proxy — yet it is still what STANDALONE_QUANTITIES compares methods on, while the C-T1 quantity (`train_times`/`avg_train_time`) is in no list.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the deviation in CONTRACTS.md's curve-key list and file it explicitly for the analysis + runner tracks: add `train_times`/`avg_train_time`/`eval_times`/`avg_eval_time` to OUTCOME_COLUMNS and STANDALONE_QUANTITIES, switch the timing comparison to `avg_train_time`, and drop the dead `val_batch`/`batch_times_val` entries from _DIAG_LOSS_KEYS.

findings.issue: Merge-order hazard: `stop_on_nonfinite=True` is the default (correct per contract) but generic_scan.py:442-507 still calls all four loops without `losses=`, and its only handler is `except Exception: print(...)` with no record written. Today a first-order blow-up wrote a NaN-curve record that style.is_diverged counted; after this change it raises DivergedError, the message is printed, and the run writes NOTHING — the local `losses` dict dies with the frame. On a ~16,000-run campaign every diverged grid point then becomes indistinguishable from never-started in reconcile.py, which is exactly the accounting C-R1/C-R2 exist to fix. Probe confirms the partial dict holds only ['batch_times_train','train_batch','val'] and none of the _finish_losses scalars, so the caller must also call summarize_curves() itself on the failure path.
findings.suggested_fix: State in the report/CAMPAIGN_STATUS that the loops must not be merged or launched ahead of the runner's C-R1, or pass stop_on_nonfinite=False from generic_scan until it lands. Also note for the runner that DivergedError subclasses RuntimeError, so its isinstance/message classifier must test DivergedError FIRST (the message is "non-finite training loss at optimizer step N", not "failed to converge").

findings.issue: _apply_log_schedule silently no-ops: `if log_schedule is not None and hasattr(optimizer, "log_this_step")`. If the sven optimizer ever renames or property-ises that attribute (it is being changed in a parallel track), the schedule is ignored without a word and every Sven step logs the full pre-cut spectrum + utr — the npz blow-up C-L1/C-L2 exist to prevent, multiplied by ~16,000 runs on Lustre. The test only proves the attribute exists in today's sven tree (test_loops_contract.py:301), so it cannot catch the rename it is guarding against.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the hasattr guard and set `optimizer.log_this_step = bool(log_schedule(step))` unconditionally when log_schedule is not None (harmless on torch optimizers), or keep the guard and raise AttributeError once with a clear message.

findings.issue: C-T1's actual requirement — torch.cuda.synchronize() immediately before the start and end reads of every batch timer — is untested. The only timing assertion (test_loops_contract.py:209 train_times <= epoch_times, train_times[0] == sum(batch_times_train[:2])) passes identically if _sync were `pass`, so a future edit that drops a sync or mis-detects the device in _cuda_active (:207) is invisible on CPU. Minor related inconsistency: _apply_log_schedule sits OUTSIDE the timed region in train_loop_standard (:619) and train_loop_jd (:850) but INSIDE it in train_loop_svd (:721).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a CPU test that monkeypatches torch.cuda.is_available -> True and torch.cuda.synchronize -> a counter, runs 2 batches through each loop with device='cpu' tensors, and asserts 2 sync calls per batch (plus 0 when is_available is False). Move the :721 _apply_log_schedule above `_sync(cuda)` for consistency.

findings.issue: _compute_acc is now dead code — no caller remains (grep over the whole repo finds only its own def and a docstring cross-reference at :246). It is precisely the mean-of-batch-means accuracy helper that F10 condemned, so leaving it in the loops region invites someone to reuse it.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete _compute_acc (and the :246 docstring reference), or move the argmax rationale comment into _correct_count and keep only that.

findings.issue: Mid-epoch (C-E4) evaluation time is measured into _TrainEpoch.eval_time, subtracted from epoch_times at :492, and then thrown away: it lands in no curve. Probe with eval_every_steps=1 shows eval_times=[0.0031] (the epoch-end evaluation only) while four mid-epoch evaluations went unrecorded, so for the one-epoch GPT-2 study (F34), where mid-epoch evaluation is the whole curve, the evaluation overhead becomes unmeasurable.
findings.suggested_fix: Either append `acc.eval_time` to a `eval_step_times` curve in _record_epoch, or add it to the `eval_times` entry and say so in the docstring.

findings.issue: summarize_curves names a curve INDEX 'val_best_epoch'. Index 0 of `val` is the untrained model, so the value is epoch+1, not an epoch (test_loops_contract.py:266 asserts 2 for a best value that was reached after epoch 1). The docstring says so, but the record schema and the F32 overfitting analysis will read it as an epoch number and be off by one. Same class of trap: 'val_last3_mean' is the mean of however many points exist when the curve is shorter than 3 (probe: num_epochs=0 gives val_last3_mean = the untrained value).
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to `val_best_index` (or subtract 1 and return -1 for "the untrained model was best"), and return None for val_last3_mean when len(curve) < 4.
